entities.name: Hagia Sophia
entities.label: Text
entities.summary: A monumental architectural masterpiece in Istanbul, originally built as a Byzantine Christian cathedral (537 CE) under Emperor Justinian I. Its massive dome (31 meters diameter) was an engineering marvel unmatched for nearly a millennium. Converted to a mosque after 1453, it served as the model for Ottoman mosque architecture and remains one of the most significant buildings in world history.
